title: A product of valuation rings has weak dimension at most one, and its fraction field product is a localization

standard_prerequisites.name: The weak-dimension-one criterion: it suffices that every finitely generated ideal be flat
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the global statement to a statement about finitely generated ideals.

standard_prerequisites.name: Valuation rings have principal ideals, and the image of a finitely generated ideal in a product factor is its tensor product with that factor
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the single generator f of I and reduces the flatness question to the ideal (e).

standard_prerequisites.name: A principal ideal generated by an idempotent is a direct summand, hence flat
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the flatness conclusion that gives weak dimension at most one.

core_obligations: Let I be a finitely generated ideal of A and use the weak-dimension-one criterion to reduce to showing that I is a flat A-module (proof lines 30657-30659).

Let I_j be the image of I in A_j, observe that I_j = I tensor_A A_j, and conclude that I -> prod I_j is surjective by the finitely generated tensor proposition, hence I = prod I_j (proof lines 30660-30664).
Since each A_j is a valuation ring, each I_j is principal, say I_j = (f_j), and hence I is generated by the element f = (f_j) (proof lines 30665-30668).

Let e in A be the idempotent with coordinate 0 or 1 in A_j according to whether f_j is 0; write f = g e with g the nonzerodivisor having g_j = 1 where f_j = 0 and g_j = f_j otherwise, and conclude that I is isomorphic to (e) as a module (proof lines 30669-30672).

Conclude that I is flat because (e) is a direct summand of A, so A has weak dimension at most 1; and observe that A -> K is a localization since K = S^{-1}A for S = prod (A_j minus {0}) (proof lines 30673-30675).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a set J, a valuation ring A_j with fraction field K_j for each j, and sets A = prod A_j and K = prod K_j, asserting that A has weak dimension at most 1 and that A -> K is a localization (source lines 30647-30654). The proof reduces flatness to finitely generated ideals: by the weak-dimension-one criterion it suffices to show that any finitely generated ideal I of A is flat (proof lines 30657-30659). It then exploits the product structure. Letting I_j be the image of I in A_j, the proof observes that I_j = I tensor_A A_j, so the natural map I -> prod I_j is surjective by the finitely generated tensor proposition, whence I = prod I_j (proof lines 30660-30664). Since each A_j is a valuation ring, each I_j is principal, say I_j = (f_j), so I is generated by f = (f_j) (proof lines 30665-30668). The substantive step identifies I with a principal ideal generated by an idempotent: taking e to be the idempotent with coordinate 0 or 1 in A_j according to whether f_j is zero, the proof writes f = g e with g a nonzerodivisor, namely with g_j = 1 where f_j = 0 and g_j = f_j otherwise (proof lines 30669-30672). Hence I is isomorphic to the ideal (e), which is flat because (e) is a direct summand of A, giving weak dimension at most 1 (proof lines 30673-30674). The final statement follows because K = S^{-1}A for S = prod (A_j minus {0}) (proof lines 30674-30675). The non-routine content is the idempotent factorisation that turns a principal ideal of the product into a direct summand.
